1	925 .claude/skills/deep-research/SKILL.md
2	---
3	name: deep-research
4	description: Literature search and retrieval across control engineering (LPV, LFR, system identification, model augmentation) and machine learning (NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR/L4DC/CoRL, physics-informed and learning-based modelling). Use for any request to find, survey, or fetch academic papers - "what's the state of the art on X", "find papers about Y", "get me that paper", "who cites Z", literature reviews, related-work sweeps. ALSO use whenever research is driven by a DOCUMENT or a described problem rather than a topic - "read docs/<file>.md and research it", "here is our problem statement, find relevant work", "what does the literature say about this", "is this novel", "has anyone solved this", or any pasted problem description. In that case step 0 (FRAME) is mandatory and runs before any query: it extracts sub-questions, seed DOIs already cited, entry points, a disqualification filter and an anti-scope, instead of compressing the document into a keyword query, which is the documented failure mode. Runs a frame-seed-expand-filter-access procedure over dblp/OpenAlex/Crossref/arXiv/PMLR/TU-e Pure instead of keyword web search, and reports a diagnostic Research Log so the procedure itself can be improved.
5	---
6	
7	# Deep Research - control + ML literature
8	
9	Every rule here is measured, not assumed. Numbers in brackets are from probe runs
10	(v1 2026-07-25, v2 2026-07-25 after a 40-query capability probe, v3 2026-07-25 after a
11	7-agent fan-out on `docs/drift-problem-statement.md`, ~330 queries; report in
12	`docs/drift-literature-sweep-2026-07-25.md`; v4 2026-08-11 after a 4-agent fan-out on
13	marginal-mode learnability, ~150 queries).
14	
15	v3 added: the fan-out hazards (shared IP, shared scratchpad, OpenAlex daily cap), the
16	`search_arxiv` replacement, the author-homepage and HAL access routes, grep-don't-page for
17	long PDFs, and two rules that exist because a frame error cost real findings (local-holdings
18	must cover `scripts/**/research/`; dblp cannot match a property).
19	
20	v4 added: the arXiv `https` fix (the documented snippet was silently returning nothing), the
21	Scholar one-quoted-phrase rule, `title_and_abstract.search` promoted from banned to
22	conditionally recommended, grep-the-code-listing for formulas, the NASA NTRS route, and two
23	step-0 rules (enumerate the theorem-prover, grep held PDFs' reference lists).
24	
25	## Windows preamble (required)
26	
27	Prefix every snippet below with `export PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8`. Without it the curl+python
28	snippets die with `UnicodeEncodeError: cp1252` the moment a title contains a non-ASCII
29	character, which for Tóth, Györök and Péni is constant. Also: `conda run python -c` rejects
30	multi-line snippets; write to a scratchpad file and run the file.
31	
32	**Never use `/tmp` for intermediate files.** `curl -o /tmp/x.html` writes a real file that
33	`ls` can see, but Windows python then raises `FileNotFoundError` on the same path
34	(`/tmp` resolves to `...\anaconda3\Library\tmp\`). Use the absolute scratchpad directory
35	from CLAUDE.md instead. Costs a turn every time.
36	
37	**In a fan-out, `mkdir` a per-agent subdirectory and work only in it.** The scratchpad root
38	is shared between sibling agents, and a collision there fails *silently and wrongly*, which
39	is worse than a crash. Measured 2026-07-25 in a 7-agent fan-out, two distinct failures:
40	a sibling's `enum.py` in the root shadowed the stdlib and broke every `python` call with a
41	circular-import error from `json`; and a sibling overwrote `cr.py` between two calls, so a
42	batch of six Crossref lookups returned confident, correctly-formatted metadata for **entirely
43	unrelated papers** (a Synfacts note, a JHEP orientifold paper) which was nearly reported as
44	findings. Name helper scripts `<agent>/<name>.py`, never `enum.py`/`json.py`/`re.py`.
45	
46	## Why this skill exists
47	
48	Keyword search fails on niche control topics. Measured: OpenAlex `search=` for "orthogonal
49	projection regularization model augmentation" returned brain tumour classification, Quantum
50	ESPRESSO and climate projections. The paper that mattered (Györök et al. 2026) was found by
51	**author-ID enumeration**, with no topical keyword at all. Authors also rename concepts between
52	papers ("projection-based regularization" 2025 -> "orthogonal-by-construction" 2026), so a
53	query written from the old vocabulary structurally cannot match the new paper.
54	**Enumeration beats matching.**
55	
56	## 0. FRAME - mandatory whenever the input is a document or a described problem
57	
58	**Trigger:** the request points at a file, pastes a problem statement, or describes a
59	situation rather than naming a topic. Examples: "read `docs/X.md` and research it",
60	"here is our problem, find relevant work", "what does the literature say about this".
61	
62	**Do NOT compress the document into a keyword query.** That is the documented failure
63	mode of this entire skill. Measured: `orthogonal projection model augmentation` returned
64	Quantum ESPRESSO and climate projections;
65	`preventing neural network from compensating physical model parameters regularization`
66	returned graph neural networks for transportation and medical imaging, 0 on-target. A
67	distilled query is the worst possible use of a rich document.
68	
69	Read the document in full, then extract these six things **before running any query**:
70	
71	| # | Extract | Why |
72	|---|---|---|
73	| 1 | **Sub-questions** | One per genuinely open question. These become the subagent fan-out. Documents often state them outright (a "what is not known" section). |
74	| 2 | **Seed DOIs / arXiv IDs already cited** | Worth more than any keyword. Feed straight into citation traversal (step 2). A document arguing with a specific paper hands you the best seed you will get. |
75	| 3 | **Entry points per sub-question** | Venue + year, author IDs, OpenAlex topic. Never a keyword string. |
76	| 4 | **Disqualification filter** | Constraints that make a result irrelevant no matter how well it matches. Report these as "found but disqualified by constraint N", not as hits. |
77	| 5 | **Anti-scope** | Explicitly closed questions. Do not return work on them. |
78	| 6 | **Vocabularies** | See below. Mandatory. |
79	
80	### Multi-vocabulary requirement (mandatory, from `tasks/lessons.md` rule 117)
81	
82	**Before any novelty or gap claim, search the same idea in at least two other fields'
83	words, and state which vocabularies you searched next to the claim.** Fields worth
84	translating into: control, machine learning, thermodynamics, navigation and estimation,
85	statistics, econometrics, applied maths.
86	
87	This is not theoretical. Three "unreported" claims were refuted in one session by
88	re-searching in another field's vocabulary: a soft one-sided power penalty was already
89	published twice, once in control words (DiLaR-Soft) and once as the Macauley bracket in
90	thermodynamics-informed ML; and a separation problem thought novel is standard practice in
91	inertial navigation under "bias observability" and "modulation".
92	
93	Also from that rule: **an abstract can invert the verdict.** One paper's abstract says
94	"constraint on the weights", reading as a hard constraint, while the body implements a soft
95	penalty. An abstract-only read produces false negatives, so downgrade, never conclude.
96	
97	### Check local holdings first
98	
99	Before searching, grep `literature/` and `docs/references.md`. A located-but-unread local
100	paper outranks any new search result. Report anything the document cites that is already
101	on disk.
102	
103	**The check must also cover `scripts/**/research/`, `scripts/**/results/` and any
104	`thread-*.md`, not just `literature/` and `docs/`.** Measured 2026-07-25: two agents
105	independently "found" Zhuang et al. (AdamW-as-prox, TMLR 2022) and reported it as the
106	headline result, while the project already held it in
107	`scripts/gantry/drift-fix-trials/research/thread-AB-optimizer-mechanics.md` items A3/A4
108	with the venue and the key equation. The frame pointed them at `literature/` only, so both
109	burned their best find on a rediscovery. Grep the whole repo for an author surname and the
110	arXiv ID before claiming any paper is new to the project.
111	
112	**Where a local note records its own verification level, carry it into the frame.** The same
113	thread had flagged the algebra `PARTIAL-FETCH` with an explicit "re-read Section 3 before
114	citing". That is a *research task the document is handing you*, and it is worth more than a
115	new query: closing it converted an unciteable claim into a verified one.
116	
117	**Read the held PDFs, and grep their REFERENCE LISTS, before running any query.** Local holdings
118	are not only a duplicate-check; they are your best seed list, and the frame should mine them
119	rather than merely subtract them. Measured 2026-08-11: the highest-value finding of an entire
120	4-agent sweep was a clause on page 1 of a paper already in `literature/`, whose own reference
121	list then handed over the decisive companion paper ("concurrent work from our group") at **zero
122	query cost**. Look specifically for `concurrent work`, `companion paper`, `see also`, `in a
123	related work`, and any self-citation: an author's pointer to their own adjacent paper is
124	better-informed than any index, because they have read both.
125	
126	Corollary for reporting: a held paper can be simultaneously "already on disk" and "the new
127	finding", when the new part is a **clause the project never quoted**. Say which it is. Two
128	different sweeps in this repo cited the same held paper for one theorem while the load-bearing
129	clause sat unread in the same abstract.
130	
131	### Output of step 0
132	
133	State the frame explicitly before querying, so the user can correct it while it is cheap:
134	
135	```
136	Sub-questions: <n, listed>
137	Seed DOIs from the document: <list>
138	Entry points: <venue/author/topic per sub-question>
139	Disqualifies: <constraints>
140	Out of scope: <closed items>
141	Vocabularies to search: <>=3 fields>
142	Already held locally: <from literature/>
143	```
144	
145	Only then proceed to step 1.
146	
147	## 1. SEED
148	
149	### dblp - best precision for both control and ML venues
150	
151	**dblp AND-matches every term.** This is the single most common way to waste a turn.
152	Measured: `model augmentation` = 1668 hits, `+identification` = 23, `+neural` = 1.
153	**Cap queries at 3 terms.** A long descriptive query silently returns 0 and looks like
154	"no such work exists".
155	
156	**dblp AND-matches TITLE words, so it cannot find a PROPERTY.** Variance, bias, conditioning,
157	stability, identifiability: these are what a paper is *about*, not what its title says.
158	Measured 2026-07-25 across a 7-agent fan-out, 9 dblp queries returned 0 useful results:
159	`truncated backpropagation variance` = 0, `rollout curriculum horizon` = 0,
160	`identifiability marginally stable` = 0, `marginal stability neural` = 0,
161	`proximal dissipativity` = 0, all genuine zeros with valid non-empty bodies. Spend the budget
162	only on **named artefacts** (a method name, a system name, `venue:CDC:+<artefact>`) and never
163	on an analytical property. With a small per-run budget, venue-scoped queries are the highest
164	value use, because they are the *only* route to recent CDC/ECC/ACC.
165	
166	```bash
167	curl -s "https://dblp.org/search/publ/api?q=<3+TERMS>&format=json&h=15" \
168	| python -c "
169	import sys,json
170	d=json.load(sys.stdin)
171	for h in d['result']['hits'].get('hit',[]):
172	    i=h['info']
173	    print(f\"{i.get('year','?')} [{str(i.get('venue'))[:26]:26s}] {i.get('title','')[:70]}\")
174	    print(f'      {i.get(\"ee\")}')
175	"
176	```
177	
178	**Venue-scoped search** via the undocumented `venue:X:` prefix. This is the only working route
179	to recent CDC/ECC/ACC/IROS proceedings, which OpenAlex cannot reach at all:
180	
181	```bash
182	q=venue:CDC:+physics      # measured 34 hits incl. ten 2024-2025 CDC papers
183	q=venue:NeurIPS:+<term>   # 131    q=venue:ICML:+<term>   # 74
184	q=venue:ICLR:+<term>      # 77
185	```
186	
187	**dblp IP-blocks after roughly 10 queries. Budget ~8 per run.** Two distinct failures:
188	early on you see empty bodies on HTTP 200; past the threshold you get **HTTP 000, 0 bytes**
189	(connection refused) on every query including ones that worked minutes before. Recovery took
190	~10 minutes; 3 retries at 3 s backoff all failed, so back off in **minutes**, not seconds.
191	
192	Neither failure is distinguishable from a genuine zero-result miss, and misreading it costs
193	real conclusions: a probe run briefly concluded `venue:L4DC:` was an invalid venue key when
194	it was simply blocked. It is valid and returns 18 hits once unblocked.
195	
196	**dblp does NOT index IFAC-PapersOnLine.** For IFAC symposia use OpenAlex source
197	`S2898405271` (29,400 works) or Crossref.
198	
199	### OpenAlex `search=` - narrow use only
200	
201	**Works only for broad, established terminology. Fails completely on niche multi-concept
202	queries.** Measured side by side, same session:
203	
204	| Query | Top-5 |
205	|---|---|
206	| `LPV system identification` | 5/5 on-target (basis functions, subspace ID, MIMO LPV) |
207	| `orthogonal projection model augmentation` | 0/5: Quantum ESPRESSO, climate projections, brain tumours |
208	
209	Worse, `search=` given a paper's **exact title** returned brain-tumour classification at
210	rank 1 and never returned the paper at all. If you know the title, use
211	`filter=title.search:<TITLE>` which returned `COUNT: 1`, exact.
212	
213	Rules: `search=` for a broad field term. `filter=title.search:` for a known title.
214	**Neither for a concept you are trying to name.** For that, enumerate (step 2).
215	
216	**Third use, and it beat every other route on one question: when the concept has a SETTLED TITLE
217	IN ANOTHER FIELD, run `title.search:` on that exact title and read the returned list for that
218	field's own extensions.** The sibling records under a known title are a cheap forward-citation
219	substitute where the citation graph is unreachable. Measured 2026-09-18:
220	`title.search:Orthogonal Gaussian process models` returned 7 and was the sole source of the only
221	genuinely new on-question paper in the run, while three Google Scholar queries on the same
222	question produced nothing.
223	
224	### `filter=title_and_abstract.search:` - banned on acronyms, RECOMMENDED on quoted phrases
225	
226	**Never on a bare acronym.** "LPV" also matches the drug lopinavir and returns oncology papers.
227	That prohibition stands unchanged.
228	
229	**But with QUOTED MULTI-WORD phrases it is a first-class discovery mechanism, and it reaches
230	things no other route in this file can.** Measured 2026-08-11:
231	`title_and_abstract.search:"marginally stable" "recurrent neural network"` returned 8 results
232	and put an exactly-on-question IEEE Trans. Cybernetics paper from 2018 at rank 1;
233	`title_and_abstract.search:"pole on the unit circle" neural` returned 2 and found a 2026
234	preprint. Neither paper was reachable by arXiv title enumeration, dblp venue scoping, PMLR
235	indexes, Google Scholar, or citation traversal, in a ~150-query sweep.
236	
237	Why it fills a real hole: it is the **only** mechanism here that reaches a **pre-2020 journal
238	paper in the ML-adjacent control literature**. Venue enumeration of NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR
239	structurally cannot see it, and dblp cannot match the property. Use it exactly when the concept
240	has a settled multi-word name in some field, and pair one quoted control phrase with one
241	free-text ML word (or the reverse) to force the cross-vocabulary intersection.
242	
243	The earlier blanket steer away from this filter was over-broad: the measured failure was
244	polysemy on short acronyms, which quoting a multi-word phrase removes.
245	
246	## 2. EXPAND - enumerate, don't match
247	
248	**OpenAlex has a shared per-IP daily spend cap. Budget it like dblp, and guard every parse.**
249	Measured 2026-07-25: a 7-agent fan-out exhausted it mid-run
250	(`{"error":"Rate limit exceeded", ..., "dailyRemainingUsd":0}`, `retryAfter` 36240 s, resets
251	midnight UTC). Two agents then lost whole query batches, and one ran **no citation-graph
252	queries at all**. Worse, the 429 body carries no `results` key, so the snippets below print
253	nothing and it reads as a genuine miss: three "no such work exists" conclusions in that run
254	were rate-limit refusals. Always parse with `d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert 'error' not in d, d`.
255	**Crossref is the drop-in substitute for metadata** (it resolved 9 of 9 with DOI, venue and
256	pages while OpenAlex was 429ing on 7 of 7).
257	
258	**Author corpus.** The highest-recall move in this skill:
259	
260	```bash
261	curl -s "https://api.openalex.org/authors?search=<NAME>&per-page=3"
262	curl -s "https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=author.id:<AID>,from_publication_date:2025-01-01&sort=publication_date:desc&per-page=25"
263	```
264	
265	**A single author's corpus is a neighbourhood, not a field.** Enumerating only a supervisor
266	returns their orbit.
267	
268	**Resolve authors from the question, not from a stored list.** Take the authors off a seed
269	paper you actually found in step 1, resolve them with `authors?search=`, then enumerate. This
270	works identically in ML and control and carries no prior about who matters.
271	
272	**When the question is about a PROPERTY of a classical estimator, enumerate the author who
273	proves theorems about it, not the author who applies it.** These are different people and the
274	frame will hand you the second kind. Measured 2026-08-11: a frame full of neural-sysid names
275	could not answer "why is the subspace horizon load-bearing for the estimated poles"; resolving
276	`Dietmar Bauer` off nothing but the shape of the question, pulling 122 works with `select=` and
277	regex-filtering locally, produced the whole answer in **one query**. Ask "who would have written
278	the asymptotics paper", then enumerate them.
279	
280	**Bonus, and it beats chasing closed DOIs: a paywalled classic's content is recoverable as
281	CITING TEXT from one open recent paper by the same author.** Bauer's 2003 and 2005 results are
282	behind Econometric Theory and Elsevier paywalls; his own 2026 gold-OA paper restates them with
283	attribution. One author-corpus enumeration plus one open recent paper recovered five closed
284	results at zero access cost. Report them as "second-hand via the author's own later paper", never
285	as read.
286	
287	**Author IDs fragment. Enumerate EVERY returned ID and union by DOI.** `authors?search=`
288	routinely returns several IDs for one person, and picking "the right one" silently halves
289	recall. Measured: `Bendeguz Gyorok` returns `A5107471352` (5 works), `A5141295088` (1),
290	`A5133717479` (1); enumerating only the largest loses two 2026 papers.
291	
292	> **Project-specific seeds - control only. Do NOT use for a machine-learning question.**
293	> Relevant only when the question is about *this thesis's area* (LPV/LFR identification,
294	> model augmentation, precision motion). For an ML question these names will actively
295	> misdirect: skip this box and use breadth mechanisms 2 and 3 below.
296	>
297	> | Author | OpenAlex ID | Works | Note |
298	> |---|---|---|---|
299	> | Roland Tóth | `A5088619613` | 394 | two other "Roland Tóth" exist; this is the control one |
300	> | Maarten Schoukens | `A5056957450` | 175 | TU/e, supervisor |
301	> | Johan Schoukens | `A5076996530` | 1006 | nonlinear sysid |
302	> | Paul M.J. Van den Hof | `A5048625929` | 446 | TU/e, identification for control |
303	> | Mircea Lazar | `A5045512282` | 444 | physics-guided / learning MPC |
304	> | Tom Oomen | `A5050892930` | 494 | TU/e, precision motion |
305	
306	### Pick the entry point from the question type
307	
308	| Question is about... | Use | Do not use |
309	|---|---|---|
310	| This thesis's area (LPV, augmentation, LFR) | the seed box above, then mechanisms 1-3 | - |
311	| Control generally | mechanism 1 (venue-year) + 3 (topic `T11236`) | the seed box |
312	| **Machine learning** | **mechanism 2 (PMLR/NeurIPS) + 3 (topic `T11206`)** | **the seed box** |
313	| A named paper's neighbourhood | citation graph from that paper's own authors | any stored roster |
314	
315	For breadth use the three mechanisms below.
316	
317	### Breadth mechanism 1: venue-year enumeration (complete, unbiased)
318	
319	Enumerate an entire proceedings rather than searching it. No keyword, no ranking bias:
320	
321	```bash
322	# IFAC-PapersOnLine 2025: measured 2,709 works
323	curl -s "https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=primary_location.source.id:S2898405271,publication_year:2025&per-page=200&cursor=*"
324	```
325	
326	Page with `cursor=*` then the returned `meta.next_cursor`. For CDC/ECC/ACC/IROS, OpenAlex has
327	no source records 2023-2026, so use dblp `venue:CDC:` instead (see step 1).
328	
329	**Crossref beats OpenAlex for venue-year completeness.** Same journal-year: Crossref
330	returned 2,957 IFAC-PapersOnLine 2025 works against OpenAlex's 2,709, i.e. 248 records
331	OpenAlex does not hold. Use it as the completeness check:
332	
333	```bash
334	curl -s "https://api.crossref.org/journals/2405-8963/works?filter=from-pub-date:2025-01-01,until-pub-date:2025-12-31&rows=0"
335	```
336	
337	**Filter regexes need a negative list.** `augment` matches "Augmented Reality" and "data
338	augmentation": 8 of 22 IFAC hits and most of 138 NeurIPS hits were that noise. Exclude
339	`augmented reality`, `data augmentation`, `image augmentation` before counting.
340	
341	**Enumerate then filter locally. Never add `search=` inside a venue filter.** Measured on
342	IFAC-PapersOnLine 2025: `filter=source,year` + `search=model augmentation physics` returned
343	**1** result from a 2,709-work pool. Pulling 800 titles by cursor and regex-filtering them
344	locally returned **16** on-topic papers from seven unrelated groups. `search=` inside a
345	narrow filter over-constrains and silently looks like "this venue has nothing".
346	
347	Same pattern for PMLR: fetch the volume page, extract all titles, filter locally.
348	Measured on L4DC v283, 120 papers enumerated, 10 on-topic.
349	
350	Bonus finding: every IFAC-PapersOnLine hit was `diamond` OA. IFAC proceedings are fully
351	open, so venue enumeration there has no access cost at all.
352	
353	### Breadth mechanism 2: PMLR volume enumeration (the ML side)
354	
355	PMLR is fully open and enumerable per volume. Verified: **L4DC 2025 = v283** (120 PDFs),
356	**L4DC 2024 = v242** (139 PDFs); volumes currently run past v336. Also ICML, AISTATS, CoRL.
357	
358	```bash
359	# titles + the REAL pdf hrefs (do not construct the URL yourself)
360	curl -s "https://proceedings.mlr.press/v283/" | grep -oE 'href="[^"]*\.pdf"'
361	```
362	
363	**Never fabricate the PDF path.** `https://proceedings.mlr.press/v<VOL>/<id>/<id>.pdf`
364	**404s** (returns 9,379 B of HTML, which pypdf rejects as `invalid pdf header: b'<!DOC'`).
365	The real pattern, verified 200 / 2,214,319 B:
366	
367	```
368	https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v<VOL>/main/assets/<id>/<id>.pdf
369	```
370	
371	Always take the href from the volume index rather than building it. A run that constructs
372	the mlr.press path silently loses the entire PMLR route.
373	
374	**NeurIPS parser** (the plausible `<li class="conference">` shape does not exist):
375	
376	```bash
377	curl -s "https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025" \
378	| grep -oE 'href="/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/[^"]+">([^<]+)</a>'   # 5,823 titles
379	```
380	
381	**Do not use OpenAlex for ML venue enumeration.** Source records exist (NeurIPS
382	`S4306420609`, ICML `S4306419644`) but are badly undercounted: NeurIPS shows 4,134 works
383	total when recent single years exceed that. Same failure class as the missing CDC/ECC
384	records. For ML venues use PMLR directly, `papers.nips.cc`, or dblp `venue:NeurIPS:`.
385	
386	### Breadth mechanism 3: topic enumeration (field-level, no keyword)
387	
388	```bash
389	curl -s "https://api.openalex.org/topics?search=<FIELD%20WORDS>&per-page=5"
390	curl -s "https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=primary_topic.id:<TID>,from_publication_date:2025-01-01&sort=publication_date:desc&per-page=50"
391	```
392	
393	Resolved: **`T11236` Control Systems and Identification** (59,135 works),
394	**`T11206` Model Reduction and Neural Networks** (71,281 works).
395	
396	**Both sort orders fail on a 59k-work topic, in opposite ways.** `sort=cited_by_count:desc`
397	on T11236 for 2025+ returned a top-10 entirely from one prolific hierarchical-identification
398	group, 8 of 10 closed, none relevant. `sort=publication_date:desc` returned MDPI *Mathematics*
399	papers, Zenodo self-deposits and a Leicester dataset record: recent low-quality deposits, not
400	the frontier.
401	
402	**Treat topic enumeration as the weakest of the three mechanisms.** Prefer venue-year
403	(mechanism 1) and PMLR (mechanism 2), which are bounded and curated. Use topics only to
404	discover venues and author names you did not know, then switch back to enumeration.
405	
406	**Citation graph.** The direction labels are counter-intuitive; these are verified empirically
407	(seed with `cited_by_count=1236` and 54 references returned 1232 and 44 respectively):
408	
409	```bash
410	# works that CITE this one (FORWARD)
411	curl -s "https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=cites:<WID>&per-page=25"
412	# works this one CITES, i.e. its references (BACKWARD)
413	curl -s "https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=cited_by:<WID>&per-page=25"
414	```
415	
416	**Resolve the PUBLISHED DOI's work ID before traversing. This is not optional.**
417	OpenAlex records of `type: preprint` carry `referenced_works: 0`, so both directions return
418	nothing. Measured on the same paper: the arXiv record `W4406318306` gave **0** references,
419	the published record `W4416435552` gave **19**, including the single most important ancestor
420	(Kon et al. 2022, the origin of the projection method) that no other query in a 45-query
421	sweep found. A 0 here means "wrong record", not "no references".
422	
423	**But first check that a published record EXISTS, or you will hunt a work ID that does not.**
424	The rule above assumes a published version is out there. Measured 2026-07-25 on
425	`arXiv:2604.18277`: both OpenAlex records were `type: preprint` with `referenced_works: 0`,
426	and Crossref had no version at all because the paper says "accepted for IFAC publication" and
427	the proceedings are not yet deposited. So: query Crossref for the title; if it has nothing and
428	every OpenAlex record is a preprint, the citation graph is **genuinely unreachable**. Report
429	that as a coverage gap and move to the paper's *stated ancestors* instead, traversing their
430	graphs (that route worked: following the seed's named predecessor gave 13 forward citers when
431	the seed itself gave 0).
432	
433	**PMLR papers have NO DOI, so the published-record rule above cannot be applied to them at
434	all.** Measured 2026-08-11 on the LRU paper (ICML 2023): the only OpenAlex record is the arXiv
435	preprint `W4362253667`, with `cited_by_count: 0` and `referenced_works: 0`, and there is no
436	ICML/PMLR record to resolve. The citation graph for a major ML paper is therefore **genuinely
437	unreachable** by this route. Do not report "nobody cites / nobody extends this" from such a
438	traversal. Substitute: traverse from a **journal or IFAC paper that cites it** (a control-venue
439	adoption paper with a real DOI), which is what finally worked, or use dblp `venue:ICML:`.
440	
441	**Forward traversal is dead at the frontier.** 2025-2026 control papers show
442	`cited_by_count=0`. Indexing lag, not a tooling fault.
443	
444	Backward traversal is also lossy where it works: 19 of ~26 references on a checked paper,
445	dropping books (Bohlin 2006 confirmed absent). `referenced_works:` is an undocumented alias
446	for `cites:`.
447	
448	## 3. FILTER - the two fields
449	
450	**Control:** IFAC-PapersOnLine (OpenAlex `S2898405271`), Automatica, IEEE TAC/TCST/TIE, CDC,
451	ECC, ACC, IROS, Systems & Control Letters, IFAC J. Systems and Control, arXiv eess.SY / math.OC.
452	
453	**Machine learning:** NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, L4DC, CoRL, AISTATS, TMLR, JMLR,
454	arXiv cs.LG / stat.ML. ML literature is far more open than control (see step 4).
455	
456	**Skip entirely - biomedical, zero yield:** PubMed, PMC, bioRxiv, medRxiv, chemRxiv,
457	Europe PMC, DOAJ.
458	
459	## 4. ACCESS
460	
461	**Every full-text success in the capability probe came through arXiv, PMLR or TU/e Pure.
462	Zero came through a publisher.** Build the plan around that.
463	
464	### Never fetch a publisher URL
465	
466	`oa_status` does **not** predict machine reachability. A `gold` OA Elsevier item returned a
467	2,703-byte JS shell; IEEE returned HTTP 202 with zero bytes. The response is indistinguishable
468	between free and paywalled content. `gold`/`hybrid`/`diamond` mean free **to a human browser**,
469	not fetchable. Go straight to `locations[]`.
470	
471	### Query `locations[]`, and use `works/doi:`
472	
473	```bash
474	curl -s "https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:<DOI>" \
475	| python -c "
476	import sys,json
477	d=json.load(sys.stdin)
478	print(d.get('title'),'|',d.get('open_access',{}).get('oa_status'))
479	for L in d.get('locations',[]):
480	    s=(L.get('source') or {})
481	    print(f\"  [{'OA' if L.get('is_oa') else '  '}] {str(s.get('display_name'))[:32]:32s} pdf={L.get('pdf_url')}\")
482	"
483	```
484	
485	`works/doi:` returns the rich record. **Do not judge accessibility from a `title.search:`
486	result row** - the same DOI can appear twice, and the first row may carry a single location
487	with `pdf=None`, which reads as inaccessible when five locations exist.
488	
489	### Resolution order
490	
491	Ordered by measured hit rate. Stop at the first route that returns a PDF.
492	
493	1. **arXiv** `https://arxiv.org/pdf/<ID>` - 100% success on every attempt.
494	2. **PMLR** `https://proceedings.mlr.press/v<VOL>/` - fully open, all PDFs listed.
495	   L4DC 2025 = **v283** (120 PDFs). Also hosts ICML, AISTATS, CoRL.
496	   NeurIPS: `papers.nips.cc`.
497	2b. **NASA NTRS - the route for the aerospace structural-dynamics corpus** (OKID, Juang, Phan,
498	   Longman, Horta; modal testing; flexible-structure and free-floating identification). The
499	   journal versions are closed Springer or AIAA, and AIAA is outside TU/e's licences (see route
500	   5), so for much of this corpus NTRS is the **only** route. Measured 2026-08-11: OpenAlex
501	   reported `10.1007/BF00941887` as `oa_status: closed`, `pdf=None`, while the NASA Technical
502	   Publication version served 2.26 MB / 66 pp first try.
503	   **Unlike PMLR and author homepages, the path here IS constructible** from the citation ID:
504	   ```bash
505	   curl -s "https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/search?q=<TERMS>"      # JSON; check downloads[].links.pdf
506	   curl -sL -A "Mozilla/5.0" -o out.pdf "https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/<ID>/downloads/<ID>.pdf"
507	   ```
508	   The `-A` matters; a bare `curl` can get a truncated stream. Prefer the
509	   `TECHNICAL_PUBLICATION` record over the `CONFERENCE_PAPER` one: in a 4-result set only two
510	   carried files and the TP was the complete one. **Caveat to report:** pre-1995 items are OCR
511	   scans, so re-verify any quotation character-exact and say the version was a scan.
512	3. **TU/e Pure** - serves the Version of Record. The HTML search at `research.tue.nl` is
513	   **403 bot-blocked**; the OAI-PMH endpoint is the only programmatic door:
514	   ```bash
515	   curl -s "https://pure.tue.nl/ws/oai?verb=ListRecords&metadataPrefix=oai_dc&set=publications:year2026:withFiles"
516	   ```
517	   (`publications:year2026:withFiles` = 1,244 records with attached full text.)
518	   Direct PDFs live at `pure.tue.nl/ws/files/<id>/<name>.pdf`.
519	   **When OpenAlex shows an OA `TU/e Research Portal` location with `pdf=None`, that is NOT
520	   unreachable.** Take the UUID from that location's `landing_page_url`
521	   (`research.tue.nl/en/publications/<uuid>`, itself 403 bot-blocked) and ask OAI-PMH for it
522	   directly; the returned record carries the real file path:
523	   ```bash
524	   curl -s "https://pure.tue.nl/ws/oai?verb=GetRecord&metadataPrefix=oai_dc&identifier=oai:pure.tue.nl:publications/<uuid>"
525	   ```
526	   Measured 2026-09-18: recovered the Version of Record of a **closed IEEE TAC 2026** article
527	   (1.4 MB, 17 pp) in one turn, with no browser route and no publisher fetch.
528	3b. **Author homepage - the route for closed economics, econometrics and statistics.**
529	   OpenAlex reports `oa_status: closed`, zero OA locations and `pdf=None` for
530	   Econometrica / Econometric Theory / Biometrika / J. Econometrics items even when the author
531	   hosts a free copy. Measured 2026-07-25: 3 of 4 closed econometrics classics resolved this
532	   way, 0 via OpenAlex or Unpaywall.
533	   **Scrape the publications index; never guess the filename.** Filenames are idiosyncratic
534	   (`I0I1discP.pdf`, `beyondLTU2.pdf`, `wp-content/uploads/2026/06/lower_risk_bounds.pdf`) and
535	   5 guessed URLs 404'd across 4 wasted turns. This is the **same rule as "never fabricate the
536	   PMLR PDF path"**.
537	   ```bash
538	   curl -sL "<homepage>" | grep -oiE 'href="[^"]*\.pdf"'
539	   ```
540	   Then walk any `?page_id=` subpages the same way. **Do not use WebFetch for the index**: it
541	   returned navigation chrome and no link list on 3 of 3 attempts on the same page where
542	   `curl | grep` returned 21 PDF hrefs, because the summarising model drops long link lists.
543	   Also try central-bank working-paper series
544	   (`federalreserve.gov/pubs/ifdp/<year>/<n>/ifdp<n>.pdf` worked first try).
545	   **Caveat to report:** these are often pre-publication versions, so quotes cannot carry
546	   journal page numbers. Say which version was read.
547	   **Measured counterexample, 2026-08-11, 0 of 1:** this route works on a personal `~user`-style
548	   page and fails on a modern **institutional profile page**. `economics.yale.edu/people/...`
549	   exposed exactly one PDF href and it was a CV, and the Cowles/EliScholar listing is
550	   JS-driven so `curl | grep` sees no links at all. So the 3-of-4 hit rate above holds for
551	   personal homepages only. When the author has no personal page, skip straight to route 5 rather
552	   than spending turns on the institutional one.
553	
554	3c. **HAL - the route for the French control corpus (Bombois, Gevers, Colin, Scorletti).**
555	   HAL bot-walls `curl` on `/document` and `/file/*.pdf` (12.5 kB HTML titled "Making sure
556	   you're not a bot!"). Check a file exists, then read it through the MCP wrapper:
557	   ```bash
558	   curl -s "https://api.archives-ouvertes.fr/search/?q=halId_s:<ID>&fl=fileMain_s,files_s"
559	   ```
560	   then `mcp__paper-search__read_hal_paper`. The API check correctly predicted which records
561	   had no attached file, saving the fetch. HAL is the primary free route for a corpus that is
562	   otherwise closed *Automatica*.
563	
564	4. **Unpaywall** - reliable OA *oracle*, weak *locator* (`url_for_pdf=None` even for OA
565	   repository entries). Pair it with OpenAlex `locations[]`.
566	   ```bash
567	   curl -s "https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/<DOI>?email=$UNPAYWALL_EMAIL"
568	   ```
569	5. **TU/e authenticated browser session** (Claude-in-Chrome) for anything still closed.
570	   Uses the user's own institutional entitlement. Covers Elsevier, IEEE, Springer and
571	   Wiley, so it reaches most remaining closed items including 2025-2026 conference papers.
572	   Boundary measured 2026-07-25: AIAA ARC returns "No Access" even with eduVPN, so TU/e
573	   holds no AIAA licence. Continue to step 6 when this route fails.
574	
575	   **Preflight, required before relying on this route.** Two independent layers must both
576	   hold, and they fail differently:
577	
578	   ```
579	   Skill(claude-in-chrome)                              # load first
580	   mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true}
581	   ```
582	
583	   | Outcome | Meaning | Action |
584	   |---|---|---|
585	   | Returns tab list | bridge up, go on to layer 2 | navigate to a known-closed DOI |
586	   | `Browser extension is not connected` | **layer 1 down**: Claude cannot reach Chrome at all | user installs/enables the extension at `claude.ai/chrome`, same account as Claude Code, may need a Chrome restart |
587	   | Bridge up but page shows a paywall/login prompt | **layer 2 down**: Chrome is not authenticated to TU/e | user signs in via TU/e library proxy or campus network |
588	   | Bridge up, page loads, but tool is blocked | site permission not granted in the extension | user grants the site in the extension UI |
589	
590	   Layer 1 being down makes layer 2 untestable. Do not report "no institutional access"
591	   when the bridge is what failed; they are different problems with different fixes.
592	
593	   **Reporting is mandatory.** If this route is unavailable for any reason, say so
594	   explicitly in the results, name which layer failed, and mark every item that would
595	   have needed it as `unreachable - browser route unavailable` rather than
596	   `unreachable`. Silently skipping step 5 makes a reachable paper look permanently
597	   closed.
598	
599	   **VERIFIED end to end 2026-07-25** on `10.1109/IROS60139.2025.11247377` (IEEE Xplore,
600	   closed, no preprint anywhere): full text of all five sections retrieved via
601	   `navigate` + `get_page_text`, including LaTeX-rendered equations. Route works.
602	
603	   Sequence that worked, and the three traps on the way:
604	   1. `Skill(claude-in-chrome)`, then `list_connected_browsers`.
605	      **Trap A:** `[]` means either *not installed* OR *installed but not signed in to
606	      the extension*. Indistinguishable, and the error text points only at installation.
607	      Signing in to Chrome is NOT signing in to the extension.
608	      **Trap B:** the bridge is startup-scoped, so an extension connected mid-session
609	      stays invisible until Claude Code restarts (`claude --continue`).
610	   2. `select_browser{deviceId}` after asking the user which browser.
611	   3. `navigate` to the DOI, then `get_page_text`.
612	      **Trap C:** anonymous IEEE returns abstract + Section I then
613	      `"Sign in to Continue Reading"`. That string is the layer-2 tell. With eduVPN or
614	      the library proxy active, the same URL returns every section.
615	   Re-navigate after the user enables VPN; the paywalled render is cached in the tab.
616	
617	   **Trap D, and it will make you misreport a working route as a paywall.** The first
618	   `get_page_text` after a `navigate` routinely returns **the abstract and the section headings
619	   only**, or errors with "No text content found", because the body has not rendered yet. There
620	   is no `"Sign in to Continue Reading"` string, so it looks exactly like entitled-but-truncated.
621	   **Call `get_page_text` a second time before concluding anything.** Measured 2026-08-11 on two
622	   separate IEEE DOIs: call 1 returned abstract only, call 2 returned every section with rendered
623	   equations. Navigating to the canonical `ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/<id>/` rather than the
624	   `doi.org` redirect also helps. Springer behaves the same way and additionally prints
625	   `Access provided by <institution>` in the body, which is the positive layer-2 tell to look for.
626	
627	   **Long full texts persist rather than print.** A `get_page_text` over ~50 kB is written to a
628	   tool-results JSON file instead of returned inline. Read it with `json.load(io.open(path,
629	   encoding='utf-8'))`, **not** a bare `open()`, which dies with `UnicodeDecodeError: charmap` on
630	   Windows. Then check for a `[output truncated at N of M characters]` marker at the tail: at
631	   50 kB of 93 kB the later sections are absent, so any "the paper never says X" claim over the
632	   unread remainder is unsupported. Say which sections were retrieved.
633	6. **MCP DOI retrieval** - if a DOI is available and every route above has failed, call
634	   `download_scihub`; if that fails, call `download_with_fallback`, preserving its upstream
635	   fallback behavior. If no DOI is known, resolve one from OpenAlex/Crossref metadata first.
636	
637	Why this order and not the reverse: routes 1-3 are the only ones that produced full text in the
638	capability probe, arXiv at 100%. Placing a low-hit-rate route first costs a failed request on
639	every paper that was freely available anyway, which is the large majority (~74% of one measured
640	corpus was legally free, and 58 of 60 titles the probe surfaced were reachable).
641	
642	### What is structurally unreachable
643	
644	- All publisher sites (Elsevier JS shell, IEEE 202), including gold OA.
645	- IEEE conference papers with no preprint (CDC/ECC/ACC/IROS are frequently closed).
646	- Elsevier articles from groups that do not self-archive. TU/e and SZTAKI papers are
647	  near-always on Pure or arXiv; other groups' often are not.
648	- Recent CDC/ECC as a browsable OpenAlex venue (no source records 2023-2026; use dblp `venue:`).
649	- Forward citations for 2025-2026 work.
650	- **Citation graphs for PMLR papers** (no DOI, preprint-only OpenAlex record; see step 2).
651	- Books in the citation graph.
652	- AIAA (no TU/e licence) **except** where a NASA-authored version exists on NTRS, route 2b.
653	
654	## 5. READ AND CITE
655	
656	**The deliverable is a citable finding.** A paper read in full through the browser and
657	correctly cited is already a complete success, so do not burn turns chasing a file you do
658	not need.
659	
660	**But if the text cannot be read, downloading is how you get it. Work the resolution order
661	all the way down, including step 6.** Never abandon a paper because reading failed;
662	a downloaded PDF is read locally with `Read`. The two are alternative means to the same
663	end, and whichever works is the right one.
664	
665	Note for either path: IEEE returns HTTP 502 to `curl` even *with* valid institutional
666	entitlement (a bot wall, separate from the paywall), and the extension blocks in-page URL
667	extraction, so a publisher-direct download attempt failing says nothing about whether other
668	routes will work. Do not treat a failed download as a failed retrieval, and never report a
669	paper as unreachable when its text was read.
670	
671	- Prefer the TU/e Pure Version of Record over a preprint when the published version matters.
672	- `Read` handles PDFs natively (`pages` for long ones).
673	
674	### Grep long documents, do not page through them
675	
676	**For any PDF over ~30 pages, extract-and-grep with context instead of reading pages.**
677	Measured 2026-07-25 on a 126-page monograph: two `pypdf` greps for `"spectral radius"` and
678	`"runcated"` with +-700 characters of context located the load-bearing assumption, the scope
679	disclaimer and the convergence theorem in two turns. Paging it would have cost 7+ turns at the
680	20-page `Read` limit and would plausibly have missed the decisive sentence entirely.
681	
682	```python
683	import sys,re
684	from pypdf import PdfReader
685	r=PdfReader(sys.argv[1])
686	for i,pg in enumerate(r.pages):
687	    t=pg.extract_text() or ""; tl=t.lower()
688	    for p in [x.lower() for x in sys.argv[2:]]:
689	        for m in re.finditer(re.escape(p),tl):
690	            a=max(0,m.start()-700); b=min(len(t),m.end()+700)
691	            print(f"=== p{i+1} [{p}]"); print(" ".join(t[a:b].split()))
692	```
693	
694	**Grep the ASSUMPTION vocabulary, not the topic**: `we assume`, `beyond the scope`,
695	`future work`, `finite variance`, `does not hold`, `spectral radius`, `if the system is`.
696	A paper's scope disclaimers are where "nobody has done this" is actually written, and they
697	never appear in the title, the abstract, or any index.
698	
699	**Sibling rule: when the deliverable is a FORMULA rather than a caveat, grep the IMPLEMENTATION
700	vocabulary and go to the appendix CODE LISTING first.** Grep for a variable name or a keyword
701	argument, never the concept word. Measured 2026-08-11 on the LRU paper: greping `normaliz`
702	returned 80 kB of prose across 30 pages and no formula, and overflowed into a truncated output;
703	greping `r_min` landed directly on the Appendix A Python listing carrying `nu_log`, `theta_log`,
704	`gamma_log` and every initialisation distribution, in one turn. Same on S4D: `S4D-Lin` hit
705	Listing 1 with `dt_min=1e-3, dt_max=1e-1`. Good probes: `r_min`, `dt_min`, `log_dt`, `init`,
706	`torch.`, `np.random`, `def `, `Algorithm 1`, `:=`.
707	
708	An exact initialisation rule is almost never in the prose. It is in a listing, an algorithm box,
709	or a hyperparameter table, and those are what the acceptance criterion "stated well enough to
710	implement" actually depends on.
711	
712	**Do not trust `file` for page count.** It reported 3 and 6 pages for arXiv PDFs that pypdf
713	read as 18 and 36, because it parses only the linearised first chunk. Two correct downloads
714	were nearly discarded as truncated. Check with pypdf; never re-download on a low `file` count.
715	- Route 5 (browser) reliably yields **text**, not **files**. `get_page_text` on IEEE returns
716	  every section including rendered equations. That is enough to read, quote and cite.
717	- **Do not conclude from an abstract.** State what you verified in full text and what you did not.
718	
719	### Citation metadata is mandatory for every paper named
720	
721	Pull it from Crossref rather than transcribing from a page; publisher pages routinely omit
722	page numbers and the venue's full name.
723	
724	```bash
725	# ready-to-paste BibTeX
726	curl -sL -H "Accept: application/x-bibtex" "https://doi.org/<DOI>"
727	
728	# structured fields (authors, venue, pages, date, type)
729	curl -s "https://api.crossref.org/works/<DOI>"
730	```
731	
732	Verified 2026-07-25 on `10.1109/IROS60139.2025.11247377`: returned a complete
733	`@inproceedings` entry including `pages={18320-18326}`, which the IEEE Xplore page does
734	not display anywhere.
735	
736	Every paper in the output needs: **authors, title, venue, year, DOI, and where the free
737	copy is.** If a field is genuinely unavailable, say so rather than omitting it silently.
738	
739	## 6. REPORT
740	
741	Findings first, then the Research Log. See the format at the end of this file.
742	
743	## Failure modes
744	
745	| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
746	|---|---|---|
747	| `UnicodeEncodeError: cp1252` | Windows console | `export PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` |
748	| dblp returns 0 on a descriptive query | AND semantics | Cap at 3 terms |
749	| dblp returns an empty body | rate transient | Retry with backoff; check for empty |
750	| OpenAlex acronym search returns medicine | "LPV" = lopinavir | Do not put a bare acronym in `title_and_abstract.search`. Quote a multi-word phrase instead, which is a recommended mechanism (step 1) |
751	| `search_google_scholar` returns a bare `[]` | 2+ `"quoted phrases"` in one query, 6 of 6 measured | Re-run the same sentence **unquoted**, or with at most one quoted phrase. Never record it as a zero |
752	| arXiv API returns nothing on a query that should hit | plain `http://export.arxiv.org` 301s with **0 bytes**; also 200-with-0-bytes under fan-out rate limiting | Use `https://` + `curl -sL` + `-w "bytes %{size_download}"`. A 0-byte body is never a zero-result answer |
753	| Publisher URL gives JS shell / 202 | bot wall, applies to gold OA too | Never fetch publisher; use `locations[]` |
754	| `pdf=None`, looks paywalled | reading a `title.search` row | Use `works/doi:`, read all `locations[]` |
755	| `cites:` returns 0 | it is FORWARD; frontier papers have no citers | Use `cited_by:` for references |
756	| Semantic Scholar returns `[]` | 429, and the MCP wrapper hides it silently | Needs an API key; treat `[]` as suspect |
757	| `research.tue.nl` 403 | bot-blocked HTML | Use `pure.tue.nl/ws/oai` |
758	| `conda run python -c` newline error | harness limit | Write a scratchpad file |
759	| `filter=title.search:` returns COUNT 0 on a title you can see exists | OpenAlex does not normalise non-ASCII punctuation; an en-dash in `Input-Output` was enough | Fall back to Crossref `query.bibliographic`, which matched the same title at rank 1 |
760	| A download succeeds (33 kB) but the parse dies with `Expecting value: line 1 column 1` | `conda run python script.py < file.json` receives **no stdin**; conda run does not forward it. Indistinguishable from an empty download | Pass the path as `argv[1]` and open it in the script |
761	| **OpenAlex returns no results, on a query that should hit** | **HTTP 429 daily spend cap. The 429 body is valid JSON with an `error` key and NO `results` key, so every parser in this file renders it as zero hits** | **Guard every snippet: `assert 'error' not in d, d`. Add `-w "\nHTTP %{http_code}"` to the curl. Fall back to Crossref** |
762	| dblp / arXiv API returns an empty body on HTTP 200 | rate transient, not a zero | Sleep 3+ s between arXiv calls; back off in **minutes** for dblp. Never record it as a zero |
763	| `file` reports 3 pages for an 18-page PDF | it parses only the linearised first chunk | Check page count with pypdf; do not re-download |
764	| Crossref metadata is confidently wrong for the DOI you asked about | a sibling agent overwrote your helper script in the shared scratchpad root | Work in a per-agent subdirectory (see Windows preamble) |
765	
766	## MCP tools
767	
768	`mcp__paper-search__*` wraps the same APIs.
769	
770	**`search_arxiv` is unusable for multi-concept queries. Use the arXiv API directly.**
771	Condemned independently by four agents in one 2026-07-25 fan-out: it matched the token "Deep"
772	in author *names* (returning papers by "Deep Pandey", "Deep Ray", "Indra Deep Mastan", 15/15
773	off-target, twice); it returned CMS/ATLAS particle physics for an **exact title**, with a
774	101 kB spill file; and it returned air-pollution LSTMs, fake-news detection and symplectic
775	4-manifold topology for a marginal-stability query, 0/15. Same failure class as OpenAlex
776	`search=`. The raw API with field prefixes and boolean AND was high-precision on nearly every
777	attempt (`ti:"proximal" AND ti:"Adam"` returned exactly 1 hit and it was the right paper;
778	`abs:"antisymmetric" AND abs:"recurrent neural network"` returned 2, both bullseyes):
779	
780	```bash
781	curl -sL -G "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query" \
782	  --data-urlencode 'search_query=abs:"<CONCEPT A>" AND abs:"<CONCEPT B>"' \
783	  --data-urlencode "max_results=15" \
784	  -w "\nHTTP %{http_code} bytes %{size_download}\n"
785	```
786	
787	**The `https` and the `-L` are load-bearing. Do not revert them to `http`.** Measured
788	2026-08-11, independently by two agents in one fan-out: plain `http://export.arxiv.org` returns
789	**HTTP 301 with 0 bytes**, or HTTP 200 with 0 bytes, and every parser here then prints nothing.
790	Both agents recorded four apparent zero-result misses before diagnosing it, and one nearly
791	reported them as novelty evidence. The `-w` line is there so the byte count is always visible:
792	**a 0-byte body is never a zero-result answer.**
793	
794	Two title terms is usually the right size; the API AND-matches like dblp. Use `ti:` for a
795	known title, `abs:` for a concept, `cat:` to scope. **Sleep 3+ seconds between calls**, or
796	three rapid queries return a silent empty body indistinguishable from a zero-result miss.
797	**Under a fan-out, 3 s is not enough.** Measured 2026-08-11: agents sharing one IP hit hard
798	429s after roughly a dozen calls each even at 4 to 5 s spacing, then kept returning 0-byte and
799	126-byte bodies on HTTP 200 through 100 s and 180 s backoffs. Budget arXiv per agent like dblp,
800	and re-run any suspicious zero individually before recording it.
801	
802	**Read `opensearch:totalResults`, because the count is itself the deliverable.** A total of
803	0 to 2 over a whole-of-arXiv abstract search is the strongest novelty evidence this skill can
804	produce, stronger than any ranked list. Measured: only **2** arXiv abstracts contain both
805	"proximal operator" and "physics-informed"; `"one-sided" AND "penalty" AND "dissipative"` = 0;
806	`abs:"port-Hamiltonian" AND abs:"lossless" AND abs:"neural"` = 0. Those zeros carried more
807	weight in the final report than most of the hits.
808	
809	**`search_google_scholar` is a MANDATORY cross-check after enumeration, not an optional
810	extra.** In a 45-query probe it was the *only* route that found OrthoReg (Richter &
811	Kilbertus, TU Munich / Helmholtz Munich, `arXiv:2606.19145`), a paper directly on the
812	physics/neural overlap problem, from a group with no link to TU/e or SZTAKI. No OpenAlex
813	query, no dblp query, no venue enumeration and no citation traversal surfaced it.
814	Enumeration and keyword search are **complementary**; neither is strictly better. Run one
815	Google Scholar query per research question after enumerating, and treat a hit it alone
816	found as a signal that the enumeration frame was too narrow.
817	
818	Confirmed at scale on 2026-07-25: it was the sole source of the highest-value item in **four
819	of seven** sub-questions, each time from a community unconnected to the seeds (computational
820	neuroscience, probabilistic numerics, computer graphics, robot dynamic-parameter
821	identification). Two distinct mechanisms, and the second is the new one:
822	
823	1. **Recall breadth**, as in the OrthoReg case above.
824	2. **It indexes full text, so it is the only route to an in-body SCOPE DISCLAIMER** - the
825	   sentence where authors say a case is out of scope, which is where "nobody has done this" is
826	   actually written. Measured: a 14-result query snippet-matched "allowing the spectral radius
827	   of the sequence to tend to 1 over time, but this is beyond the scope of the present work"
828	   on p24 of a 126-page arXiv monograph. No OpenAlex, dblp, arXiv or Crossref query in the
829	   same run could reach it.
830	
831	So when the question is "has anyone treated case X", **write the Scholar query as the sentence
832	you expect the paper to contain**, not as keywords. And note the vocabulary traps: Scholar's
833	"proximal" space is owned by Proximal Policy Optimization (13 of 15 hits were RL).
834	
835	**Write the sentence, but quote at most ONE phrase in it.** This is the other half of the rule
836	above and without it the route silently dies. Measured 2026-08-11 across two agents: every query
837	containing two or more `"quoted phrases"` returned a bare `[]` (6 of 6), while long *unquoted*
838	descriptive sentences on the same topics returned 10 to 15 results and were the sole route to
839	four separate top-tier findings. One quoted phrase plus free words is the shape that works.
840	**A multi-phrase `[]` is "rephrase", never "nothing"**: it is indistinguishable from a rate
841	limit, so re-run it unquoted before recording any zero. Confirmed at scale in the v4 run: of
842	the 4 sub-questions, Scholar was the sole source of the single most on-point paper in 3.
843	
844	**Counter-measurement, 2026-09-18: Scholar returned 0 on-target across 7 sentence-form queries
845	in a 2-agent sweep, on a question about a GEOMETRIC CONDITION.** Both agents wrote them as
846	sentences with at most one quoted phrase, per the rules above, and got digital twins, magnetometer
847	calibration, XRF spectroscopy, credit-risk symmetry, proper orthogonal decomposition and MDPI
848	"physics-based" noise. The concept had no settled cross-field name, so full-text snippet matching
849	had nothing to latch onto. **Qualify the rule:** run Scholar when hunting a scope disclaimer or an
850	unconnected community; expect it to fail on questions whose keywords are shared with a dominant
851	unrelated method (POD, PPO, "physics-based", "orthogonal"), and cap it at 2 queries before
852	abandoning rather than spending the budget.
853	
854	**`search_core` is a usable locator**, contrary to earlier text: it returned a working
855	direct PDF link (14 pp, 2.38 MB) for a paper it found. Precision is poor (4 of 5 off-target),
856	so use it to *locate* a known paper, not to discover.
857	
858	**`search_semantic` returns `[]` masking an HTTP 429.** Confirmed against the raw API. A `[]`
859	means "unknown", never "nothing". Dead weight until a key is set.
860	
861	## Subagent fan-out
862	
863	One agent per independent seed or sub-question. Do not spawn for a single lookup. Give each
864	agent the sub-question, known author IDs / seed DOIs, the field filter, and an instruction to
865	return findings plus its Research Log. Merge logs, deduplicate by DOI.
866	
867	**Every agent shares one IP and one scratchpad, so tell each of them, explicitly, in the
868	prompt:**
869	- a **dblp budget** (2 queries at 7 agents, 2 to 3 at 4 agents; the IP blocks after ~10 for
870	  ~10 minutes, and a 503 mid-run means a sibling spent theirs first),
871	- an **OpenAlex budget** and the `assert 'error' not in d` guard (the daily spend cap is
872	  shared and a 7-way fan-out exhausts it). Measured 2026-08-11 at 4 agents: ~12 each never came
873	  near the cap, and the four agents together spent under 40, so 12 to 18 each is safe at this
874	  width,
875	- an **arXiv budget too**, which v3 omitted and which cost the v4 run three planned novelty
876	  counts: the API 429s per-IP after roughly a dozen calls per agent even at 4 to 5 s spacing.
877	  Tell them to print the byte count and never record a 0-byte body as a zero,
878	- to `mkdir` and work in a **per-agent scratchpad subdirectory**,
879	- **not** to run the TU/e browser preflight. One preflight belongs in the parent; seven
880	  agents each asking the user which browser to use is a bad experience. Have them mark items
881	  `needs-browser-route` and chase the ranked list from the parent afterwards.
882	
883	**Set the frame before fanning out, and show it to the user.** The agents inherit whatever
884	scoping error it contains, multiplied by N. Measured 2026-07-25: a frame that named
885	`literature/` as the local-holdings location caused two of seven agents to spend their best
886	find rediscovering a paper the repo already held.
887	
888	**Ask each agent to grade its own negative claims.** A "nobody has done this" from an agent
889	whose OpenAlex calls were 429ing, or whose venue sweep reached 30% of one year, is provisional
890	and must be reported as such. Merge those caveats into the final report rather than dropping
891	them; a gap claim is only as strong as the coverage behind it.
892	
893	## Required output format
894	
895	```markdown
896	## Findings
897	<answer to the question. For EACH paper: authors, title, venue, year, DOI, and where the
898	 free copy is. State its actual finding, not just that it exists. Include BibTeX for
899	 anything worth citing.>
900	
901	## Access status (MANDATORY - every run, even when nothing was paywalled)
902	TU/e browser access: AVAILABLE | UNAVAILABLE (<which layer failed>)
903	<If UNAVAILABLE, state it plainly in the visible answer, not only here. Any item that
904	 would have needed it is marked "unreachable - browser route unavailable", never a bare
905	 "unreachable". If AVAILABLE and used, say which papers came through it.>
906	
907	## Evidence quality
908	<read in full vs abstract-only vs metadata-only - be explicit>
909	
910	## Research Log
911	- Queries run: <source + query + n results + on-target?>
912	- What worked: <the query shape that produced the find>
913	- What failed: <query/source that returned noise or errors, and why>
914	- Dead ends: <looked relevant, was not>
915	- Coverage gaps: <what this sweep could NOT reach>
916	- Suggested skill fix: <concrete change to this SKILL.md, or "none">
917	```
918	
919	Search, do not recall. Every paper named must come from a query run in the session; if
920	something came from repo files instead, say so.
921	
922	**Always report the TU/e browser access status**, on every literature run, not only on
923	probes and not only when something turned out to be paywalled. The user needs to know
924	whether the run had institutional access available, because a sweep done without it has a
925	systematically different reachability profile: closed Elsevier and IEEE items silently drop
926	out and the result looks complete when it is not. State it even when every paper was open.
927
